translations.answer: The paper reduces single-GPU, massively parallel off-policy locomotion training to about fifteen minutes and demonstrates G1/T1 deployment. That number does not cover its more expensive whole-body tracking experiment and does not replace robot identification, domain randomization, or repeated hardware acceptance tests.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Training hardware, parallel-environment count, network, and hyperparameters are close to the paper's locomotion recipe.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Platform-specific identification of robot dynamics and actuators, plus domain randomization, has been completed.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Velocity-command walking on G1/T1; whole-body tracking is a separate, more expensive experiment
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper supplies wall-clock curves, cross-robot hardware demonstrations, and public code. The fifteen-minute title applies only to the locomotion setting on one RTX 4090, and no large repeated hardware success-rate table is reported.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Sections 3-5, Figures 1-7, Tables 1-2, and the appendix
translations.evidence.0.note: Separates the budget for fifteen-minute single-GPU locomotion from multi-GPU whole-body tracking and reports sim-to-real deployment.
translations.evidence.0.title: Learning Sim-to-Real Humanoid Locomotion in 15 Minutes
translations.terms.4: Graphics Processing Unit (GPU, 图形处理器)
translations.title: Does 'training in 15 minutes' mean any humanoid whole-body task can be trained on one consumer GPU and deployed reliably in fifteen minutes?
